task.title: File attachments should accept drag+drop
task.description:
Allow people to attach files to a task by providing a drop target around the file attachment controls so that a user can drag a file from their Finder onto the web app to attach.

## Shipped (2026-08-16, PR #109)

One PR through a two-round adversarial execution-verified review (record on the PR), browser evidence from real Chrome over CDP with genuine OS-backed File objects (OS-level Finder drags aren't scriptable; the event dispatch is synthetic, stated honestly throughout).

Both attachment surfaces - the task view's panel and the create form's staging area - are now drop targets, routing dropped files through the acceptFiles seam PR #106 built, so every ceiling pre-check applies to drops by construction. One dropDecision(event) answers dragenter, dragover, and drop (the Blink accept-flag class); file drags are preventDefault-ed EVEN WHEN REFUSED because an unhandled file drop navigates the window and destroys staged Files, with refusal shown as a distinct red state carrying its message. DataTransfer.types discrimination runs both ways: card drags don't light the file zone, and the board's dragDestination/drop gained draggingFiles guards after finding that a stale card-drag state would let a dropped FILE move an unrelated CARD (reproduced through a real API write with the guards reverted). Folders are detected via webkitGetAsEntry and named rather than staged-then-failed; child-churn flicker uses the board's own two-question rule.

The review's blocker was structural: the original refusal message lived in a drop handler Blink never calls - dropEffect "none" makes Blink CANCEL the drag (dragenter, dragover..., dragleave, no drop), so a busy-drop vanished silently and the red outline stuck permanently; the fake-DOM test passed only by invoking the listener directly. Fixed by announcing refusal at decision time. The companion stuck-highlight bug closed with a two-deadline timer (250ms armed only by an ambiguous leave; 3s idle backstop) after the implementer measured the review's suggested watchdog wrong: a cancelled drag delivers the page NOTHING and a paused hover emits no further dragover - the same fact that forced the board onto a frame loop. Final matrix 17/19 with both survivors benign and one re-pinned post-approval (with its own honest correction: the obvious assertion didn't discriminate; the guard's unique effect is keeping handler notes off a panel an active run is using).

Residuals (accepted): Firefox/Safari untested - the only place the 250ms grace is load-bearing; no per-file fan-out on multi-file drops (acceptFiles stops at the first refusal, per #106's contract, stated plainly in the record); paste-to-attach noted as the obvious sibling, not filed.
